newsitem.title: USA: Consumer electronics to boost 97 chip sales - report.
newsitem.headline: Consumer electronics to boost 97 chip sales - report.

text.p: The market for seminconductor chips used in consumer electronics is expected to rebound from its 1996 decline and grow to $27 billion in 1997, according to market resesearch firm Dataquest.
The technology research firm said revenues for the consumer electronics chip market fell $1.9 billion to $24.2 billion in 1996 from $26.1 billion in 1995.
In addition, Dataquest projected that the market would grow to $45.7 billion in revenues by the year 2000.
While the consumer electronics market represents only a fraction of the $300 billion chip industry in the year 2000, the segment is expected to be one of the fastest-growing.

Dataquest said that although the consumer electronics semiconductor market struggled in 1996, the market should rebound in 1997 with the emergence of both next-generation and digitally enhanced consumer electronics.

Next-generation consumer electronics include digital set-top TV boxes, video game consoles, new devices that combine compact disc and videocassette features, digital cameras, video CD players and high-definition TV receivers.

Digitally enhanced consumer electronics products are products that have been enhanced by the addition of new digital technology. Some examples are camcorders that now employ motion compensation and digital zoom, and TVs with integrated TV guide systems.

"Because of the establishment of industry standards for most of these products, analog, digital, and mixed-signal... products are expected to find extremely high growth opportunities," said Dale Ford, senior industry analyst for Dataquest's Semiconductor Applications Markets program.

"The poor showing for consumer electronics sales during 1996 has created a sense of urgency among consumer electronics companies working to employ new technologies to revitalize a slumping industry," said Ford.
These chips will be used to create the enhanced audio, video and graphics features that marketers hope will wow buyers into a new wave of consumers electronics purchasing.

"At the recent Winter Consumer Electronics Show, leading industry executives revealed that their future plans rely on recapturing consumer interest in their core products by adding digital enhancements to legacy products and by pushing the development of a new category of advanced consumer electronics."

It said consumer electronics based on older designs such as standard color TVs, portable stereos, and VCRs will find buyers in the mid- to low-end segments, but chip shipments in these products will remain relatively flat.
